official.citizenship_residency: Candidates with Norwegian citizenship or international citizenship. International applicants who do not reside in Norway apply by 1 March; Norwegian citizens and international citizens enrolled in a Norwegian high school or resident in Norway apply by 15 April and submit their final diploma by 7 July. For scholarship purposes BI defines an international applicant as a candidate with international citizenship who moved to Norway to undertake post-secondary studies.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is open to candidates with international citizenship as well as Norwegian citizenship, and international applicants who apply for it are also considered for the Bachelor International Scholarship and the Women in Finance and Tech Scholarship if eligible. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay the higher non-EEA tuition rate of NOK 138,400 per year, which the scholarship would also cover.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to applicants who receive an offer of admission in the Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Data Science for Business or Bachelor of Digital Business programme; applicants to Bachelor of Data Science for Business must additionally document the mathematics requirement.
official.duration: Up to three years of 100% tuition fees, conditional on academic progression (three-year, 180 ECTS full-time bachelor programmes taught in English in Oslo)
official.description: Awarded to applicants who graduate with the top grades from the International Baccalaureate (IB) programme, this entrance scholarship covers 100% of tuition fees for up to three years if the student maintains the academic progression requirements for scholarship recipients. Candidates with the highest IB grades are competitive and the minimum grade for consideration is 33 IB points, final or predicted, together with an offer of admission to one of BI's three English-taught bachelor programmes. Scholarships are awarded on academic excellence, not financial need, and recipients act as BI Ambassadors.
official.region: Europe (Norway) - BI's three eligible international bachelor programmes are taught in English in Oslo
official.program_type: Merit-based entrance scholarship covering 100% of tuition fees
official.english_requirement: IB applicants who passed English A with grade 3 or above or English B with grade 5 or above from the IB Diploma Programme fulfil BI's English proficiency requirement; all other IB students must submit a test. Accepted tests: TOEFL ibt (including home edition) overall 80 or above, IELTS Academic overall band 6.0 or above, Pearson PTE Academic (including online) overall 59 or above, telc English B2-C1 University, Cambridge B2 First (overall B), C1 Advanced (overall C) or C2 Proficiency, or University of Michigan ECPE or ECCE with overall band score 840 or above. English proficiency test score reports older than 2 years are not accepted.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a pure merit prize for IB graduates with 33 points or more who hold an offer for one of BI's three English-taught bachelor programmes in Oslo, and it removes tuition entirely - NOK 106,400 a year, or NOK 138,400 if you hold citizenship outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland - for up to three years. Nothing else is funded: BI's own estimate for living in Norway is about NOK 151,690 a year, which you must cover from family funds, savings or loans, so treat this as a tuition waiver rather than a full ride. The decision is made at the moment you apply, because the scholarship has to be attached to the same admission application submitted by 1 March if you live outside Norway or 15 April if you are Norwegian or resident, with the final diploma following by 7 July. Strong candidates get a second bite automatically: the same application feeds BI's Bachelor International Scholarship and Women in Finance and Tech competitions at no extra cost.
applicant_utility.best_fit: IB graduates with 33 or more points, especially from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland where wiping out the NOK 138,400 non-EEA rate is worth the most.
application_readiness_checklist: Build the package before the portal opens on 1 November: a single PDF holding your CV plus a one-page (strictly maximum) letter on why you deserve the award, plus your predicted-grade statement if you are still in the IB.
Ask your IB coordinator to release your results through the IBO database to BI's institute number 000609 so your final July grades reach BI without you chasing them.

Check your English route immediately: English A grade 3+ or English B grade 5+ exempts you from a test, otherwise book TOEFL, IELTS or PTE at least a month before the deadline, and make sure the result is less than two years old.
Work out which tuition band your citizenship puts you in, then budget the gap plus living costs on BI's published figures before you commit.
Accept the offer of admission as soon as it arrives - scholarship offers travel separately, in late April and again in July, and you cannot hold your place waiting for one.
Plan your visa funding proof in parallel if you need a residence permit: non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants need all documentation in by 15 June.
common_rejection_risks: Sitting on the 33-point minimum instead of competing on your whole record: BI says candidates with the highest IB grades are competitive and also weighs other academic, extracurricular and personal achievements, and the applicant pool far exceeds the number of awards.

Uploading the CV and the letter as two files, or as an email attachment - the portal only counts one combined PDF in the Scholarship section of the admission application, and email applications are refused outright.

Filing an incomplete admission application: the scholarship is only considered if a complete admission application exists, and nothing can be added after submission, so a missing passport scan, motivation letter or financial plan kills the scholarship claim too.
Reading '100% tuition' as a full scholarship and then failing the residence-permit funding proof or dropping below 30 ECTS per semester and a cumulative B in a later year.

Assuming the award can be moved to a different BI programme or held for another intake - it is tied to the named programme, and only one scholarship per applicant is awarded no matter how many you apply for.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs of roughly NOK 151,690 per year on BI's own estimate, plus course literature and support materials, re-sit examination fees (NOK 330 per credit for 2026/27), travel and accommodation for any programme trips, and the mandatory Student Welfare Organisation membership fee. Students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland who do not win the scholarship face the full NOK 138,400 annual rate; the fee is invoiced per semester and adjusted annually.
document_audit: The IB transcript and diploma must be the IBO-issued documents, not your school's report; if you are in your final year you need an official predicted-grades statement, and BI asks you to enable IBO database access to institute 000609.
The scholarship letter is capped at one page and must be merged with the CV into one PDF - splitting them or exceeding the page limit is the most common avoidable failure on this award.

Documents must be official and in English or a Scandinavian language; anything else needs a certified translation alongside the original, and BI rejects electronic diplomas in favour of a scan or photo of the paper original.

International applicants must also complete BI's personal financial plan template showing how tuition and living costs will be funded, which overlaps with the UDI living-expense proof for the study permit.
Portal uploads must be PDF, JPG, JPEG or PNG and under 25 MB, so compress colour scans of diplomas and passports before the deadline day.
alerts: The deadlines are admission deadlines, not a separate scholarship round: 1 March if you do not reside in Norway, 15 April if you are a Norwegian citizen or an international citizen enrolled in a Norwegian high school or resident in Norway (final diploma by 7 July). Late and emailed applications are never considered.

BI awards only one scholarship per applicant, but applying for the IB scholarship automatically enters you for the Bachelor International Scholarship and Women in Finance and Tech Scholarship with no extra letter - so use that one submission well.
Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants need all documentation submitted by 15 June to allow time for the student residence permit; missing that date costs the place even with top grades.
Scholarship decisions are final and cannot be appealed, and only successful applicants are notified - silence means no award, so keep funding alternatives alive until you see the offer.
The scholarship survives only while full progression does: 30 ECTS every semester and a cumulative BI-scale GPA of at least B, plus BI Ambassador duties when asked.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission does everything: complete the admission application on BI's portal (opens 1 November), attach the combined CV-plus-letter PDF in the Scholarship tab, upload every admission document, then accept the admission offer and sign the study contract while waiting for a separate scholarship decision in late April or July.
